title: mime-tree/walk.rs: compute_body_structure should be pub(crate), not pub inside private module
description:
Why this exists: mime_tree/src/walk.rs is a private module (mod walk in lib.rs, not pub mod walk). The function compute_body_structure inside it is declared pub, which makes it pub(crate) in practice — but the intent is not explicit. The Rust coding standard prefers explicit pub(crate) over relying on the private-module rule to limit visibility.

What goes wrong: if walk.rs were ever made pub (e.g. during refactoring), compute_body_structure would accidentally become part of the public API. The explicit pub(crate) annotation documents the intended scope and would cause a compile error if accidentally widened. The BodyStructure type in the same module is already correctly annotated pub(crate).

Location: mime-tree/src/walk.rs, fn compute_body_structure.

Fix: change pub fn compute_body_structure to pub(crate) fn compute_body_structure.
close_reason: compute_body_structure is pub inside a private module — it's effectively pub(crate). Adding the explicit qualifier is cosmetic.
